findings.heading: #### Follow-up data / #### Dữ liệu theo dõi
findings.proposition: The English says each contact is supposed to have an encounter each day for 14 days after exposure, with no counterparty named; the Vietnamese adds 'với ca mắc' and states the daily encounter is with the case.
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader concludes the follow-up records are daily meetings between the contact and the index case, so they misread the whole followups dataset: rows are contact-tracer check-ins on a quarantined contact, not repeated exposures. That inverts the meaning of followup_status ('seen with/without symptoms') and of the 14-day quarantine logic used later in the chapter.

findings.heading: #### Follow-up data / #### Dữ liệu theo dõi
findings.proposition: The English states that each row of followups is a follow-up interaction; the Vietnamese states that each row is a contact who was followed up ('mỗi hàng là một người tiếp xúc được theo dõi').
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader treats the row count of followups as a count of contacts, not of encounters. That contradicts the de-duplication section beside it, which counts several rows per contact per day, and it makes the later per-contact summarise() step look redundant.

findings.heading: ### Import data / ### Nhập dữ liệu
findings.proposition: The English keeps the knitr::include_graphics() call for images/godata_api_github.png inside an HTML comment, so no image is shown; the Vietnamese has the same chunk uncommented, so it renders a screenshot of the Go.Data API GitHub page.
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader sees an unexplained screenshot with no caption or referring sentence, and the page carries a figure the English page does not. If images/godata_api_github.png is absent the Vietnamese chapter fails to render while the English one builds.

findings.heading: ### Data cleaning / ### Làm sạch dữ liệu
findings.proposition: The English calls each follow-up record an 'encounter', with no channel specified; the Vietnamese calls it 'cuộc gọi truy vết' (a tracing phone call) and asks whether the call took place, thereby asserting that follow-up is done by telephone.
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader takes telephone contact as the definition of a follow-up encounter and may treat in-person or SMS visits as outside the dataset, mis-specifying followup_status categories when adapting the code to their own data.
